methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $36M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Hystar, a Series B–stage climate and energy company that has raised $36M to date, is valued here against a competitive set of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Linamar, LNZA). The peer universe includes established frontier-energy players such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy, all in Series C with valuations ranging from $700M to $3.0B.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy, applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $68M. Peer-median analysis draws from three same-sector, same-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.0B and a range of $700M–$3.0B, reflecting wide dispersion in market expectations for climate-tech businesses at this stage.

Triangulation across these two methods produces a broad valuation range of $58M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $534M. The wide interval reflects material uncertainty around Hystar's relative technology maturity, market timing, and capital efficiency versus peers. The peer-median method dominates the high end of the range given the substantial valuations of comparable-stage competitors, while stage-progression anchors the conservative bound. Key uncertainties include the company's unit economics, path to commercialization, and whether peer valuations reflect durable competitive advantages or sector-wide froth.
